isolation_fix.defect: AC5_DegradedOrderLifecycle PASSED in isolation (npx playwright test geo.spec.ts) but FAILED in the full serial suite (npm run e2e) at geo.spec.ts:154 — expect(freeName, 'a Free known-password driver is available for the assign').toBeTruthy() received undefined. Root cause: the chromium project runs analytics → dispatcher → geo (alphabetical, 1 worker, shared DB); by geo's turn the seeder's Free drivers were consumed/absent and the old code scanned listDrivers for ANY Free known-password driver, which returned nothing.
isolation_fix.seeded_driver_reality: DevelopmentSeeder: driver1 Jan Novák (vehicle1) — Free at seed, Assigned to DEMO02 (Assign does NOT change DriverStatus) + Completed DEMO05 → net Free, consumed by dispatcher.spec/customer.spec. driver2 Petr Svoboda (vehicle2) — Free then Assigned+Accepted DEMO03 → Busy, consumed by driver.spec. driver3 Karel Dvořák (vehicle3) — seeded Offline then brought online-with-vehicle3 and driven to InProgress on DEMO04; NOT touched by any other chromium spec.
isolation_fix.fix: Added a test.describe.serial beforeAll (ensureGeoDriverFree) that makes geo's OWN deterministic Free driver — Karel Dvořák (driver3), the one seeded driver no other chromium spec touches and which the seeder leaves online-with-vehicle (mid-ride, not offline, so it keeps its vehicle3). It releases the driver's non-terminal orders: InProgress → Complete via the driver API (Cancel is ILLEGAL from InProgress per OrderStateMachine line 104; Complete sets DriverStatus→Free per line 333), Arrived → Start+Complete, New/Assigned/Accepted → Cancel via the dispatcher; then getMe-asserts status=Free, currentVehicleId!=null, activeOrderId==null. AC5 now assigns to THAT named driver (asserts geoDriver.status==='Free' by name, failing loudly) instead of scanning for any Free driver. Resolved driverId/name via listDrivers (never hardcoded). Rewrote the stale header comment (was claiming a runtime-Free guarantee the old code did not deliver).
isolation_fix.no_offline_online_route: Deliberately did NOT use the 'offline-then-online' recipe the task text suggested: goOnline(session, vehicleId) needs a vehicleId, and for an OFFLINE driver getMe.currentVehicleId is null and listDrivers only returns the plate — so there is no way to obtain the vehicleId. driver3 is seeded online-with-vehicle3 (only mid-ride), so completing its ride returns it to Free WITHOUT ever going offline, keeping vehicle3. This mirrors the driver.spec beforeAll pattern (cancel-non-terminal-then-assert-Free), adapted for an InProgress order that must be Completed rather than Cancelled.
isolation_fix.no_contamination_of_later_specs: geo drives its OWN fresh order to Completed (releasing driver3 to Free again), and driver3 is not pre-depended-on by the later mobile-driver (driver2) or mobile-customer (driver1) projects. Verified empirically: the full-suite run shows all 3 mobile-driver + all 5 mobile-customer tests green after geo.
